data.title: Amazon Stock (AMZN) Is Falling on Tuesday – Here's Why
data.description:
Amazon (AMZN) said Tuesday that it cannot restore access to certain customer data stored in parts of the Persian Gulf after several of its cloud facilities were damaged during the U.S.-Iran war. The company shared the update on its Amazon Web Services (AWS) health page, noting that the affected information was hosted only in data centers in Bahrain and in parts of its network in the United Arab Emirates. Following the news, AMZN stock was down about 2% on Tuesday.

AWS said the Bahrain sites were hit early in the conflict, with damage beyond what the company's systems were built to handle. Satellite images later showed strikes on two facilities there.

Most customers in Bahrain shifted their workloads to other countries after the first strikes in March, and further damage in April wiped out the remaining data center network in the country. In the UAE, Amazon said many customers were able to restore operations by using backups or copying data that stayed reachable. However, the company still cannot access data stored in one UAE availability zone, and engineers are working to recover resources in two others.

Other Factors Pressuring the Stock

On the logistics side, Amazon filed an 8‑K with the SEC saying it has paused work with air carrier 21 Air. The move follows a deadly crash of an Amazon‑branded cargo plane in Miami. The pause only affects a small slice of Amazon's Prime Air network, but active federal safety probes add short‑term shipping and reputational pressure that is weighing on the stock.

Further, the wider tech sector is under pressure after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned that frontier AI work is slowing. That comment hit harder for Amazon, which recently raised its full‑year 2026 capex guide to $220 billion, most of it aimed at AI data centers and custom chips.

With spending now running far above earlier plans, investors are concerned that such huge cash outlays may take longer to produce real returns.

Is Amazon a Buy or Sell Right Now?

Overall, Wall Street has a Strong Buy consensus rating on Amazon stock, based on 39 Buy and one Hold recommendations issued in the past three months. The average AMZN stock price target of $334.28 indicates 34.43% upside potential.

data.title: Why Is DataMeds AI Stock (MEDS) Up Nearly 200% Today?
data.description:
DataMeds AI (MEDS) stock rocketed higher on Tuesday after the health IT company announced its acquisition of a business from Axe Compute (AGPU). Axe Compute sold its legacy cancer diagnostics business, Helomics Corporation, to DataMeds AI. The deal moves Helomics out of Axe Compute as the company completes its shift to a pure-play neocloud GPU-as-a-Service business.

Under the terms of the deal, Axe Compute sold its wholly owned Helomics unit in return for DataMeds AI common shares and common share equivalents. Helomics is a Pittsburgh-based precision medicine platform focused on cancer care. The company uses AI and real-world tumor data to aid drug discovery and cancer treatment choices. Helomics was the last operating business left from Axe Compute's prior identity as Predictive Oncology Inc. Axe Compute changed its name in December 2025 as part of its move toward AI compute services.

The sale also gives DataMeds AI a new role in oncology. The company claimed that the deal adds Helomics' cancer data and AI tools to its platform. DataMeds AI said it plans to use its data-driven approach to help improve patient outcomes in an area with a high need for better care.

data.title: Target (TGT) to Challenge on Amazon's Fall Sales Event
data.description:
Discount retailer Target (TGT) is looking to challenge Amazon's (AMZN) autumn Prime Days sales event. Minneapolis-based Target has announced that its fall "Circle Deal Days" event will run Oct. 6–7 in a direct challenge to Amazon's "Prime Big Deal Days" shopping extravaganza. Target said in a statement that it will offer discounts of up to 40% on thousands of products during he October event.

Target's promotions will cover fall apparel, home décor, kitchen tools, beauty products, toys, technology, and holiday merchandise. The biggest discounts will be offered to Target Circle 360 members, who can begin shopping select offers on Oct. 5. Target added that its strategy with the fall sales event is to attract budget-conscious seasonal shoppers.

Taking on Amazon

Target (TGT) is also using the upcoming event to drive subscriptions to its Target Circle 360 loyalty rewards program. The autumn sales event has evolved from Target Circle Week, a longer loyalty-sale format. In October 2025, Target held a seven-day Circle Week sales promotion that featured discounts of up to 50% and daily deals. That event proved popular with consumers.

data.title: Dow Jones Today: DJIA Stumbles as 10-Year Treasury Yield Reaches 5%; Oil Climbs
data.description:
The Dow Jones (DJIA) is down 0.82% on Tuesday as Treasury yields continue to rise. The 10-year yield is up 3.9 basis points to 5%, marking its highest level since 2007. With higher yields, the opportunity cost of holding equities rises, as investors may shift their capital toward virtually risk-free government bonds. In addition, higher yields increase borrowing costs and reduce the present value of future cash flows.

Elevated oil prices have helped drive yields higher. Brent crude oil (BZ) is up 2.5% to $108.30 per barrel and has risen 38% since the onset of the U.S.-Iran war on February 28. Higher oil prices raise inflation expectations, which pushes investors to demand higher bond yields.

With inflation remaining above the Fed's target of 2% for over five years, the Fed is likely to raise interest rates tomorrow with a 92.5% probability, according to the CME FedWatch tool. Last Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 3.4% for the 12 months ended August.

data.title: Robinhood Stock (HOOD) Drops 4% as Two Employees Charged with Fraud
data.description:
The stock of online brokerage Robinhood Markets (HOOD) is down 4% after the U.S. Attorney's Office for New York charged two of the company's employees with fraud. Robinhood engineers Hefu Chai and Huaisong Xiang were each charged with commodities fraud and wire fraud arising from a scheme to misappropriate confidential business information from the company.

The stolen information was allegedly used to trade perpetual futures on the decentralized derivatives exchange called "Hyperliquid." According to the complaint filed in Manhattan federal court, Chai and Xiang had access to nonpublic information related to whether and when Robinhood will support additional cryptocurrencies for trading.

The two used that information to make profitable bets on Hyperliquid, according to the lawsuit.

data.title: Boeing Stock (NYSE:BA) Gains With Multiple Defense Contracts
data.description:
Aerospace stock Boeing (BA) is on a roll. It has landed multiple defense contracts that should represent stable income and help give the commercial aircraft space room to breathe. This was welcome news for investors as well, who gave Boeing shares a fractional boost in Tuesday afternoon's trading. Boeing has seen a 2.21% loss in its share price over the past year.

New Ceiling, Old Contract

One of the biggest wins in defense contracts for Boeing came from the KC-46 contract between Boeing and the United States Air Force. That contract already existed, but it was modified to have a new maximum value: up to $19.1 billion, which allows for increased foreign sales.

This meant an additional $13.4 billion in value was added to the contract from its original amount. With the new contract, Boeing can sell to Japan, Israel, and other countries that have yet to be named, "future partners," noted a report from Investor's Business Daily.

With this, the Navy will have access to an unmanned tanker system, the first of its kind for the navy so far. It also serves as the Navy's first operational unmanned aircraft that works from a carrier. With this tool in place, the Navy can continue using its F/A-18 Super Hornet aircraft, and keep fighter jets from being used as air-to-air refueling systems.

data.title: Rivian vs. Lucid: One EV Stock Looks More Like the Next Tesla, Says Investor
data.description:
Tesla's rise from a niche electric car maker to a company worth more than $1 trillion offers an important lesson for investors hunting for the next big EV winner. Elon Musk's original strategy was straightforward: start with an expensive, desirable vehicle, use the cash and experience gained to move into cheaper models, and eventually reach a mass-market audience.

That strategy took years to play out, but it gave Tesla the manufacturing scale, cash generation and brand recognition needed to pursue bigger opportunities such as autonomous driving and robotaxis.

Following in Tesla's wake, both Rivian (NASDAQ:RIVN) and Lucid (NASDAQ:LCID) are trying to establish themselves as major EV players, but they are taking rather different routes. And with Rivian valued at roughly $23 billion vs. ~$1.60 billion for Lucid, the two stocks offer very different risk-reward profiles.

Investor Ryan Vanzo, who contributes to The Motley Fool, believes that for those looking for a potential Tesla successor, one of them is a far more likely candidate to give the EV leader a run for its money.

The difference between the way these companies are going about their business is particularly clear when looking at the latest vehicle launches. Lucid's Gravity SUV is positioned firmly at the luxury end of the market, with a starting price of almost $126,000. Once options, taxes and other costs are included, buyers could easily be looking at more than $150,000.

That may help Lucid build a premium brand, but it does little to solve one of the biggest challenges facing an EV startup: achieving the volume necessary to build a sustainable business.

Rivian's strategy looks very different. Its R2 SUV starts at roughly $45,000, with more expensive versions reaching around $60,000. That puts the vehicle much closer to the price range of mainstream consumers. Rivian also plans to follow the R2 with the cheaper R3 and R3X, giving it a potential path toward much greater production volumes.

Vanzo argues that this puts Rivian closer to the playbook Tesla used to build its business. Lucid has lower-priced vehicles in development too, but its planned mass-market model has already been pushed back from 2026 to late 2027, raising questions about how quickly it can expand beyond the luxury market.

The same advantage might extend to autonomous driving and robotaxis. Both companies are developing self-driving technology, but Rivian's much larger market value gives it considerably more financial firepower. Vanzo notes that Rivian could raise an amount greater than Lucid's entire market cap through only a relatively small amount of shareholder dilution.

There is also evidence that outside companies see value in Rivian's manufacturing ambitions. Uber has agreed to purchase as many as 50,000 R2 vehicles as it builds out its robotaxi plans. Its separate agreement with Lucid covers 35,000 vehicles.

That does not guarantee Rivian will succeed, and Uber is clearly spreading its bets. Still, Vanzo sees the larger commitment to Rivian as another indication that the company is better positioned to supply vehicles at scale while developing the software needed for autonomous driving.

For investors willing to accept the risks of an unprofitable EV maker, Vanzo therefore sees Rivian as the more compelling choice. "Despite a higher valuation, Rivian shares look more attractive given the company's larger manufacturing scale, low-cost model launches, and a seemingly more advanced self-driving tech platform," the investor summed up. The Street, however, does not seem to be enamored with either EV maker, as both claim Hold consensus ratings.
